text:
Maya: Hey team — need approval for a capacity bump on project `redwood-pilot`. Customer pilot looks like it will need ~12x A100 (80GB) for evals + ~8x L4s for inference bursts. Also need a small H100 pool for long-tail perf tests. Can we get GPU quotas + a pool of static EIPs for ephemeral nodes? Timeline: pilot opens next Wed.

Sam: Region? billing host project? any shared-VPC constraints? :thinking_face:

Maya: Primary region = us-west1, failover = eu-west4. Billing host = `infra-billing-prod`. This will run in our shared VPC so we need the service account `svc-redwood-pilot@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` added to `Network Admin` for the host project. Need ~10 static EIPs for NAT/external allocation.

Jordan: Suggest mixing H100 for heavy tail + A100 + L4 for cost efficiency. Maybe 4x H100 + 8x A100 + 8x L4 instead of 12x A100. Gives better latency for the worst-case and cheaper steady-state.

Leo: Quick cost sketch: 4xH100 reserved ~= $YYk/mo, 8xA100 on-demand bursts ~= $ZZk/mo, 8xL4 spot ~= $aaK/mo. If we do preemptible A100 for batch evals we can cut ~40% off the A100 line. I put numbers in the drive doc: https://drive.google.com/some-doc (internal).

Maya: Filed the internal quota form here: https://go/infra-quota?ticket=Q-4521&project=redwood-pilot — please review + sign. Also a quick gcloud check you can run: 
```gcloud compute project-info describe --project=redwood-pilot --format="json"
gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --project=redwood-pilot
```

infra-bot: quota-ticket #Q-4521 created, assignee: Sam, status: awaiting cloud-ops approval. ETA SLA: 3 business days.

Sam: I'll kick off the cloud-ops approval and attach the network preflight. We need finance approval for > $60k/mo recurring. @Amy FYI for budget sign-off. I'll also ask cloud-ops to reserve the EIP pool in us-west1 and eu-west4 and to enable shared VPC host project scoping.

Amy: ACK — will review the cost sheet today and respond by EOD. :thumbsup:

Sam: @Jordan can you add a fallback routing plan to cut over to hosted Redwood API if local capacity falls below 20%? That will keep customer SLAs during provisioning hiccups.

Jordan: Yep — plan is model-variant fallback + autoscale cap + prefix caching. I'll paste the rollout snippet in this thread after I finish.

Maya: Thanks all. If we can get infra + finance sign-off by EOD tomorrow we can queue the provisioning for Monday and hit the pilot date. Ping me if you need any extra perms or cost detail. :pray:
